definitions.gloss: detour; dawdling; loitering on the way
definitions.explanation: Stopping or lingering along the way instead of going directly to one's destination. Often used with する or {食|く}う. Originally referred to a horse stopping to eat grass on the roadside.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{道草|みちくさ}をして{帰|かえ}りが{遅|おそ}くなった。
examples.english: The child dawdled on the way and got home late.

examples.japanese: {道草|みちくさ}しないでまっすぐ{帰|かえ}ってきなさい。

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly used in the set phrase {道草|みちくさ}を{食|く}う (to dawdle, literally "to eat roadside grass"). Can also be used with する. Typically describes children loitering on the way home from school, but applies to anyone making unnecessary stops.

ETYMOLOGY:
From {道|みち} (road) + {草|くさ} (grass). Originally described a horse stopping to graze on grass along the road during a journey, delaying the traveler.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {道草|みちくさ}を{食|く}う (to dawdle on the way)
- {道草|みちくさ}する (to loiter, to make detours)
